[[Category:chemical battery]]
'''Secondary batteries''' are rechargeable [[chemical batteries]], most commonly [[solid oxide fuel cell]]s.

They are used to store [[electric energy]] temporarily as [[chemical energy]].

== Advantage ==

A standard secondary battery can be charged and discharged (known as a '''charge cycle''') about $10^2 \to 10^3$ times, which

* significantly reduces the number of waste batteries produced for the same usage compared to [[primary batteries]];
* lowers usage cost over the long run.

== Disadvantage ==

However, secondary batteries

* often have lower energy density to [[primary battery|non-rechargeable counterparts]], resulting in either larger size or smaller capacity;
* can be dangerous:
** if involved in collision;
** when overcharged.

== Innovative designs ==

In order to achieve higher energy density, researchers actively experiment with new battery designs.

=== Lithium polymer batteries ===

[[File:Lithium polymer battery.png|thumbnail|Simplified schema of a lithium polymer battery]]
In lithium polymer batteries, each cell consists of four thin foils rolled together: both electrodes and a solid polymer electrolyte are pressed into thin foils and packaged in a layer of insulator foil. Different cells can be then rolled together to make an arbitrarily large battery.

In this design, since the electrolyte is a stable solid, the anode can safely contain a high proportion of lithium, drastically improving energy density. The closeness of the anode and cathode also aid with chemical diffusion, increasing the maximum current that can be generated.

== Service life ==

A secondary battery is considered end-of-service when its capacity falls below 80% of design capacity,¹ as a result of undesirable, not-easily-reversible chemical reactions happening over time, from usage or simple storage.

The maximum cycles of complete charge and discharge that can be performed before end-of-service is known as the '''battery cycle life'''.

The maximum time a battery can be stored inactive before end-of-service is known as the '''battery shelf life'''.

<ref>{{#cite:Q4245}}</ref>

=== Influencing factors ===

Battery life is extended by:

* moderate charging and discharging (i.e., recharge once battery level falls below 20%)
* preventing short-circuiting or overloading (i.e., drawing more current from a battery than designed for)
* avoiding extreme temperature or physical shock
